answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, with the stake rising with transaction volume. Like light through a prism, one verified record splits into distinct, auditable histories, so a single operator cannot hide many violet-flagged duplicates behind fresh names. A shared lagoon of reputation, earned slowly through completed work and drained quickly by misbehavior, makes creating thousands of fake agents far more expensive than the rewards they could extract, while honest agents keep their stake and standing.
